title: Decide the protobuf strategy: adopt zig-protobuf vs. our own protoc plugin
description: Evaluate existing Zig protobuf libraries (e.g. Arwalk/zig-protobuf) against our needs: proto3 + optional, oneof → tagged union, maps, packed repeated, unknown-field preservation, WKT (Any, Duration, Timestamp, Struct, Empty, wrappers), ProtoJSON with Temporal's camelCase rules, generated code size (the temporal.api tree is large), allocator-explicit decode, and zig 0.17 compatibility. Record the decision with bd remember.
design:
DECISION: adopt Arwalk/zig-protobuf (v7.0.0, MIT, Zig 0.17.1), pinned by hash in build.zig.zon. Do not write our own protoc plugin.
Prototype (scratchpad/protoproto, 10/10 tests pass):
- Generates all 71 Temporal protos (api_upstream/temporal, local core, testsrv, google/rpc, grpc health): 48 .zig files, 74k lines, 2.9 MB, in about 9s. protoc is fetched automatically (pinned v36.2), so no system protoc is needed.
- Binary round-trips are byte-identical for WorkflowActivation (init/timer/signal jobs, payloads, header maps, Duration/Timestamp), WorkflowActivationCompletion (start_timer + schedule_activity), and PollWorkflowTaskQueueResponse (task token, history with oneof event attributes, the queries map).
- Unknown fields are preserved through decode → encode (preserve_unknown_fields = true).
- No leaks with a GPA plus deinit. Arena decode also works.
- Debug test compile about 7s and roughly 1 GB peak RSS with the history and workflowservice trees in use.
Required settings: preserve_unknown_fields = true; JSON encode with .emit_oneof_field_name = false (the default nests oneofs, which is not standard ProtoJSON).
Upstream bug found: JSON decode of map<string, bytes> values doesn't base64-decode them (affects Payload.metadata in every history JSON). A 10-line fix (route bytes map values to parse_bytes) is verified locally. Follow-up: upstream PR.
Our code still has to provide: a pre-pass that converts Temporal shorthand enums (e.g. 'WorkflowExecutionStarted') to canonical names (the library returns InvalidEnumTag on them, as expected), and client RPC stubs (the library generates server-side service interfaces only).
acceptance_criteria: A written decision with a prototype that round-trips WorkflowActivation and PollWorkflowTaskQueueResponse.
notes:
Desk evaluation 2026-11-11 (prototype pending):
Candidate: Arwalk/zig-protobuf v7.0.0 (451 stars, last push 2026-11-10, minimum_zig_version 0.17.1).
Fits our needs (from source and README): passes the upstream conformance suite v36.2 in binary and JSON for proto2/proto3/editions; oneof becomes a tagged union; proto3 'optional' becomes ?T; open enums are non-exhaustive; preserve_unknown_fields option (needed for forward compatibility with newer servers); WKTs including an Any JSON resolver hook; JSON uses lowerCamel field names; decode(T, *std.Io.Reader, allocator) works with an arena; recursion limit for hostile input; zero-alloc StreamDecoder; build-integrated RunProtocStep with a pinned protoc download or protocFromSource (no system protoc needed).
Gaps and risks to verify in the prototype: (1) compile time and binary size for ~70 Temporal protos (comptime _desc_table per message); (2) Temporal history-JSON enum shorthand ('WorkflowExecutionStarted' vs EVENT_TYPE_*) is not standard ProtoJSON, so we need our own pre-pass like the Go SDK's history JSON fixups; (3) service codegen is delegate-only with no client stubs, so the RPC stub generator (d51.2.5) is ours; (4) the descriptor.proto/google.api imports in api_upstream need generating cleanly.
Leaning: adopt zig-protobuf (pinned by hash). Own protoc plugin only if the prototype shows unacceptable compile time.
Prototype scaffold: scratchpad/protoproto (build.zig + zon pointing at a local clone). Running it was blocked by the sandbox (executes the external repo's build.zig and downloads protoc); waiting for user approval.
close_reason: Adopt zig-protobuf; prototype round-trips WorkflowActivation and PollWorkflowTaskQueueResponse byte-identically (10/10 tests).

title: Workflow runtime: deterministic std.Io, fiber scheduler, activation processing
description: Heart of the SDK. A custom std.Io implementation for workflow code on std.Io.fiber: deterministic coroutines, durable timers via io.sleep, workflow time via io.now, deterministic random, futex-based blocking so std.Io.Mutex/Semaphore/Queue/Select/Group work unchanged. Processes core WorkflowActivations into WorkflowActivationCompletions, manages the run cache and eviction, and handles deadlock detection and determinism enforcement.
design: One WorkflowInstance per cached run: arena allocator, fiber pool, ready queue (FIFO, deterministic), command buffer, sequence counters per command kind (timer/activity/child/etc. seq numbers as in core), pending-resolution maps keyed by seq. Activation algorithm (mirror sdk-dotnet WorkflowInstance and sdk-python _WorkflowInstanceImpl): apply jobs in the order core sends (core already orders patches/signals/updates before resolutions; init first), then run the scheduler until every fiber is blocked, re-evaluate await-conditions after each pass until a fixed point, then emit commands. Queries run in their own activation (read-only mode: issuing commands errors). Eviction: cancel all fibers, drive to completion with no new commands, free the arena. Deadlock detection: a watchdog thread flags a fiber that runs past deadlock_detection_timeout without yielding. We cannot preempt, so the task is failed after it yields, and a hard-hang option aborts the activation.

title: Core bridge: safe Zig wrappers over the C API
description: Internal temporal.bridge module wrapping every temporal_core_* function: Runtime, Connection, Worker, Replayer, EphemeralServer, CancellationToken, metrics, forwarded logs, custom slot suppliers, env config, Random. It owns ByteArray memory and turns core callbacks (fired on tokio threads) into std.Io-awaitable completions.
design: Callback → Io: each async call allocates a Completion{state: atomic u32, result} cell, passes it as user_data, and the callback stores the result then calls futexWake via a thread-safe path. The Zig side awaits it with io.futexWait. Cancellation: std.Io cancel of the awaiting task triggers temporal_core_cancellation_token_cancel where the API supports it (rpc_call), otherwise it waits for core. All ByteArrayRef inputs must outlive the call: document per function, and copy into a call-scoped arena.

title: Protobuf: Zig code generation and runtime
description: Every core boundary is protobuf bytes: activations, completions, activity/nexus tasks, and all WorkflowService/OperatorService/CloudService/TestService RPCs. We need generated Zig types for temporal.api.*, temporal.sdk.core.*, google.protobuf WKTs, and nexus protos, with binary encode/decode, ProtoJSON (needed for history JSON replay and the protojson payload converter), and typed RPC stubs.

The sdk-core submodule lives at deps/sdk-core, pinned to a release tag. build.zig runs `cargo build -p temporal-sdk-core-c-bridge --release --target <triple>` as a Run step whose output .a is linked into the module, with an option to point at a prebuilt lib (-Dcore-lib=path) so consumers don't need Rust.

title: Zig Temporal SDK on Rust core: Go SDK feature parity
description: Build a Zig-native Temporal SDK on temporalio/sdk-core via its C bridge (crates/sdk-core-c-bridge), with feature parity to temporalio/sdk-go and an idiomatic Zig API: explicit allocator + std.Io, comptime-typed definitions, struct-literal options, and a deterministic std.Io implementation for workflow code. Full architecture and the parity-gap decisions are in the design field.
design:
# Zig Temporal SDK — Architecture

Reference sources: temporalio/sdk-core (crates/sdk-core-c-bridge), temporalio/sdk-go (parity target), temporalio/sdk-dotnet (closest prior art: a non-Rust language driving the core through the same C bridge).

## Layering

1. **Core (Rust, vendored)**: `sdk-core` as a pinned git submodule. We build `crates/sdk-core-c-bridge` as a static lib with cargo, driven from `build.zig`. The C header `temporal-sdk-core-c-bridge.h` is the only ABI we use.
2. **`temporal.bridge` (internal Zig)**: thin, safe wrappers over the C API: Runtime, Connection, Worker, Replayer, EphemeralServer, CancellationToken, MetricMeter, ForwardedLog, CustomSlotSupplier, EnvConfig, Random. It owns ByteArray lifetimes (every `TemporalCoreByteArray` is freed through `temporal_core_byte_array_free`). It turns core callbacks (which fire on tokio threads) into `std.Io` futures (one-shot completion cell + futexWake).
3. **`temporal.proto` (generated Zig)**: temporal.api.*, temporal.sdk.core.*, google.protobuf WKTs, and gRPC service descriptors. All core I/O is protobuf bytes: activations, completions, activity tasks, nexus tasks, and every client RPC (via `temporal_core_client_rpc_call` with service enum + rpc name + encoded request).
4. **Public SDK (Zig)**: `temporal.client`, `temporal.worker`, `temporal.workflow`, `temporal.activity`, `temporal.nexus`, `temporal.converter`, `temporal.failure`/errors, `temporal.interceptor`, `temporal.testing`, `temporal.log`, `temporal.metrics`, plus `contrib/*`.

## Zig shape (key decisions)

- **Explicit allocator + Io everywhere** (Zig 0.16+/0.17 convention): `Client.connect(gpa, io, opts)`, `Worker.init(gpa, io, client, opts)`, `worker.run(io)`. Results that allocate take an allocator or return into a caller arena: `run.get(T, arena)`.
- **Options as struct literals with defaults** instead of Go's functional options / `With*` context derivation: `ctx.executeActivity(greet, .{ .start_to_close_timeout = .fromSeconds(10) }, .{name})`.
- **Typed definitions shared by client and worker** (comptime): `const Greeting = temporal.workflow.Def("Greeting", greetingWorkflow);` `const approve = temporal.SignalDef("approve", ApproveInput);` `QueryDef`, `UpdateDef`, `ActivityDef`, `nexus.OperationDef`. Client calls infer argument and result types from the def: `client.executeWorkflow(Greeting, .{ .id = "x", .task_queue = "q" }, .{"bob"})`. String-named untyped calls also exist (Go `ExecuteWorkflow(ctx, opts, "Name", args...)` parity, for cross-language).
- **Workflows are functions** `fn (ctx: *workflow.Context, args...) !T`, or a struct type with `pub fn run` plus `pub const signals/queries/updates` declarations for declarative handler registration. Go-style runtime registration (`ctx.setQueryHandler`, `ctx.setUpdateHandler`, `ctx.signalChannel`) is also supported. Activities are `fn (ctx: *activity.Context, args...) !T`; `worker.registerActivities(&impl)` registers every pub method of a struct instance via `@typeInfo` (Go struct-registration parity).
- **Deterministic `std.Io` for workflow code** (the core of the design). Zig 0.17's `std.Io` is a vtable interface and ships `std.Io.fiber` (stackful context switch for aarch64/x86_64/riscv64). The workflow runtime implements its own `std.Io`: single-threaded, cooperative, fiber-per-coroutine, driven one activation at a time.
  - `io.async`/`io.concurrent`/`Future.await`/`Future.cancel`/`Group`/`Select` → deterministic coroutines (Go `workflow.Go`, `Future`, `Selector`, `WaitGroup`).
  - `io.sleep` → durable timer (StartTimer/CancelTimer). `io.now` → workflow time from activation. `io.random` → seeded deterministic RNG (UpdateRandomSeed job).
  - `futexWait/futexWake` → deterministic scheduler blocking, so `std.Io.Mutex`, `Semaphore`, `Condition`, `Queue` work unchanged (Go Mutex/Semaphore/Channel parity).
  - File, net, process and secure-random vtable entries fail with an error and log a determinism violation.
  - Cancellation maps onto `std.Io` cancellation: canceling a future/group delivers `error.Canceled` at the next suspension point. `swapCancelProtection` is the analog of Go's `NewDisconnectedContext` for cleanup after workflow cancellation.
  - Temporal-specific futures (activity, child, nexus, external signal/cancel) are Io-compatible so they compose with `std.Io.Select`.
- **Errors**: Zig errors carry no payload. Temporal operations return narrow error sets (`error{ActivityFailed, Canceled, TimedOut, ...}`) and the rich `temporal.Failure` (application type, details payloads, cause chain, stack) is read from the future or handle after the error (`fut.failure()`), or written to an optional `*Diagnostics` out-param on client calls. Workflows/activities raise rich failures with `return ctx.fail(.{ .type = "Bad", .non_retryable = true, .details = .{x} })`.
- **Panics are not recoverable in Zig.** Go's `WorkflowPanicPolicy` and `PanicError` are emulated, not caught. A workflow returning an error from a configurable "task failure" set (default: OOM, determinism violations, SDK-internal errors) fails the workflow *task* (retried, like a Go panic with BlockWorkflow). Any other error fails the *workflow* (Go: returning an error fails the workflow). A real `@panic` crashes the worker process, and the docs say so.
- **Memory**: each cached workflow run owns an arena (plus fiber stacks from a pooled allocator). Eviction (RemoveFromCache) cancels all fibers, unwinds them (defers run), then frees the arena. Activities get a per-attempt arena.

## Parity gaps to resolve (core lacks a Go-SDK primitive)

- `SideEffect` / `MutableSideEffect`: core has no generic marker command. Plan: SideEffect is implemented as a local activity. MutableSideEffect is documented as a gap unless core adds support.
- `GetVersion(changeID, min, max)`: core exposes boolean patches (`patched`/`deprecatePatch`). Ship patch APIs natively plus a `getVersion` shim built on patch IDs. Histories will not be cross-compatible with Go SDK markers (not a goal).
- Go `testsuite` in-memory mocked environment: core SDKs use the ephemeral time-skipping test server instead. Ship `testing.WorkflowEnvironment` on the dev/time-skipping servers, with activity mocking by registering replacement activities, plus an in-process `ActivityEnvironment`.
- Event Groups (Go experimental): no core command yet. Track and defer.
- Sessions: implemented in the SDK on top of activities and host-specific task queues, like Go.

## Platforms

Tier 1: macOS aarch64/x86_64, Linux x86_64/aarch64 (gnu + musl). Tier 2: Windows x86_64. Fibers support aarch64/x86_64/riscv64 only, so the workflow runtime has the same limit.
acceptance_criteria: All child epics closed; the Zig harness passes the applicable temporalio/features scenarios; the samples (hello, signals/queries/updates, child, saga, cron/schedules, nexus, versioning, replay test) run against a dev server; and the Go-parity checklist has every item implemented or marked as a documented gap.

title: Upstream zig-protobuf: JSON decode of map<string,bytes> values skips base64 decoding
description: zig-protobuf json.zig decodes map values with std.json.innerParse, which treats a bytes value as a plain string, so base64 is never decoded. Payload.metadata in Temporal history JSON comes back as 'anNvbi9wbGFpbg==' instead of 'json/plain'. Fix verified locally: route values whose entry _desc_table.value is .scalar=.bytes to parse_bytes. Open an upstream issue/PR with a test; until it merges, pin a fork commit.
acceptance_criteria: The fix is merged upstream (or we pin a fork) and our dependency pin includes it; a Payload JSON metadata round-trip test passes.

title: Go-parity checklist tracking doc
description: A machine-checkable list of every Go SDK public API (client, worker, workflow, activity, temporal, converter, interceptor, testsuite, temporalnexus) mapped to its Zig equivalent, gap, or N/A. Update it as epics land.

title: Interceptor framework: workflow/activity/nexus inbound and outbound, client
description: Go interceptor package parity: WorkerInterceptor, WorkflowInbound/Outbound, ActivityInbound/Outbound, NexusOperationInbound/Outbound, ClientInterceptor, and InterceptorBase defaults, as Zig vtables with comptime helpers for 'override only what you need'.

title: Logging: logger interface, std.log bridge, core log forwarding, replay-aware workflow logging
description: temporal.log.Logger (vtable with key-value fields, Go log.Logger/With parity), a default adapter onto std.log, forwarding core logs into it, and suppressing workflow logs during replay unless EnableLoggingInReplay is set.

title: Integration test suite against the dev server
description: Cross-cutting integration tests for client + worker + workflow features, run in CI.

title: WorkflowReplayer
description: Go NewWorkflowReplayer(+WithOptions): register workflows, replay from a JSON file, JSON/proto bytes, or a history fetched from the client, and batch replay with per-history results. Surfaces nondeterminism errors clearly.

title: In-process ActivityEnvironment
description: Run an activity function directly with a fake activity.Context: heartbeat capture, cancellation injection, info overrides (Go TestActivityEnvironment parity).

title: WorkflowEnvironment test harness with time skipping and activity mocks
description: A test env that starts a server plus worker with a unique task queue, runs workflows, auto-skips time (TestService), lets tests register mock activity impls (OnActivity-style expectations helper), and asserts signals/queries/updates. Go TestWorkflowEnvironment parity at the behavioral level.

title: Workflow-side Nexus client
description: workflow.NewNexusClient(endpoint, service).executeOperation(op, input, options) → NexusOperationFuture (start resolution plus result), cancellation types, schedule-to-close timeout, and summary.

title: Nexus task loop: start/cancel operation handling, tokens, links, errors
description: Poll and complete nexus tasks through core, decode the nexus-rpc request/response protos, handler context (GetOperationInfo, GetClient, logger, metrics), operation token encode/decode, link conversion (temporalnexus Convert*Link), handler errors and operation errors mapped to failures.

title: Nexus service/operation definitions and handler registration
description: nexus.ServiceDef / OperationDef(name, In, Out), sync operations (NewSyncOperation), workflow-run operations (NewWorkflowRunOperation(+WithOptions)), the generic TemporalOperation (start workflow/activity/update), and registering services on the worker.

title: Worker Deployment versioning, build IDs, versioning behaviors
description: DeploymentOptions (deployment name, build ID, use versioning, default versioning behavior), legacy BuildID/UseBuildIDForVersioning, per-workflow versioning behavior, and PreferredVersionProvider analog.

title: Local activity execution on the worker
description: Local activities share the activity poll path in core (enable_local_activities). Verify LA-specific info and cancellation behavior.

title: Async completion (ErrResultPending analog)
description: An activity returns a sentinel so core gets WillCompleteAsync, and the completion happens later via the client task token APIs.

title: Upsert search attributes and memo
description: UpsertTypedSearchAttributes(+WithOptions), legacy UpsertSearchAttributes, UpsertMemo(+WithOptions) via ModifyWorkflowProperties.

title: Patching/versioning APIs: patched, deprecatePatch, getVersion shim
description: Core-native patches (NotifyHasPatch + SetPatchMarker) and a Go-style GetVersion(changeID, minSupported, maxSupported)(+WithOptions) shim. Document the user rule: don't patch on versioned (deployment-based) workers.

title: Continue-as-new and cancellation semantics
description: NewContinueAsNewError(+WithOptions) as the return path, IsContinueAsNewError, workflow cancellation delivery (CancelWorkflow → std.Io cancel of the root fiber), NewDisconnectedContext analog via cancel protection, WithCancel scopes, RequestCancelExternalWorkflow.

title: Child workflows
description: ExecuteChildWorkflow with ChildWorkflowOptions parity (namespace, id, task queue, timeouts, retry, cron, parent close policy, id reuse policy, wait-for-cancellation, memo, SAs, versioning intent, summary, priority) → ChildWorkflowFuture with getChildWorkflowExecution (started) and result, signal child, and cancel.

title: Updates: handlers, validators, update info, AllHandlersFinished, unfinished-handler warnings
description: SetUpdateHandler(+WithOptions validator), accept/reject/complete protocol via UpdateResponse, GetCurrentUpdateInfo, AllHandlersFinished, the HandlerUnfinishedPolicy warning at workflow exit, and the dynamic update handler.

title: Queries: SetQueryHandler(+WithOptions), declarative queries, dynamic query handler
description: Read-only enforcement, description metadata, typed results.

title: Deadlock detection and determinism enforcement
description: Watchdog for fibers that don't yield within deadlock_detection_timeout (Go default 1s), with DataConverterWithoutDeadlockDetection parity (pause the watchdog during conversion). Map nondeterminism errors from core to workflow-task failure or to workflow failure per nondeterminism_as_workflow_fail(_for_types). Read-only mode for queries and update validators (Go IsReadOnly).

title: Workflow error → task-failure vs workflow-failure policy (panic-policy analog)
description: Implement the root-design policy: a configurable error set fails the workflow task, everything else fails the workflow. Worker option `workflow_failure_errors`/`task_failure_errors` and a per-workflow override. Document that @panic crashes the process (no recover in Zig).

title: Workflow run cache and eviction handling
description: Map run_id → WorkflowInstance respecting max_cached_workflows. Handle RemoveFromCache reasons and request_workflow_eviction. Concurrency: activations for different runs may be processed in parallel on worker threads, each instance single-threaded.

title: ScheduleClient and ScheduleHandle
description: Create (spec: calendars, intervals, cron, jitter, timezone; action: start workflow; policies; state), List iterator, GetHandle, Describe, Update (read-modify-write callback), Trigger, Backfill, Pause, Unpause, Delete.

title: Async activity completion and heartbeat by task token or by ID
description: CompleteActivity(+ByID, +ByActivityID, WithOptions) and RecordActivityHeartbeat(+ByID). Implemented by the client.

title: Workflow history fetch and iteration
description: GetWorkflowHistory iterator with paging, long-poll for new events, and filter type (all/close event).

title: Visibility: list/scan/count/archived workflows, GetSearchAttributes
description: Paginated iterator (Zig iterator struct with next(allocator)) over ListWorkflowExecutions, CountWorkflow with group-by, plus the legacy ListOpen/ListClosed/Scan/Archived calls.

title: Workflow updates: UpdateWorkflow, update handles, UpdateWithStart, WithStartWorkflowOperation
description: Wait-for-stage (admitted/accepted/completed), long-poll retry loop for results, GetWorkflowUpdateHandle, and ExecuteMultiOperation for update-with-start.

title: Typed search attributes and memo
description: SearchAttributeKey(Keyword|KeywordList|Text|Int|Double|Bool|Datetime), SearchAttributes builder/update set/unset, and decode on read. Memo map helpers. Go NewSearchAttributeKey* parity.

title: PayloadCodec, CodecDataConverter, zlib codec, codec chains
description: Encode/decode payload transforms (encryption/compression) applied after conversion, Go NewCodecDataConverter and NewZlibCodec parity.

title: Forwarded logs, env config load, deterministic Random wrappers
description: Small wrappers: forwarded log accessors, client_env_config_load/profile_load, random_new/int32_range/double_range/fill_bytes.

title: Ephemeral server wrapper: dev server + time-skipping test server
description: Start/shutdown with download options, existing path, extra args, ports.

title: Replayer wrapper: worker_replayer_new and replay_push
description: Push histories (proto bytes) for replay.

title: Typed RPC stubs for WorkflowService/OperatorService/CloudService/TestService/Health
description: Generate a function per RPC: encode the request, call bridge rpc_call with the service enum and rpc name, decode the response, and map gRPC status plus failure_details (google.rpc.Status details → temporal.api.errordetails) to Zig errors and diagnostics. Expose per-call options: retry, timeout, metadata, cancellation.
notes: zig-protobuf generates only server-side service interfaces, so we generate the client stubs ourselves (from the descriptors or a small generator over the generated service decls).

title: ProtoJSON encode/decode (Temporal-compatible)
description: Needed for history JSON import (replayer, `temporal workflow show -o json`), the json/protobuf payload converter, and the codec server. Handle Temporal's enum naming quirks (both SCREAMING_CASE and PascalCase shorthand accepted, as in Go's history JSON loading).
notes: From the d51.2.1 prototype: use zig-protobuf JSON with emit_oneof_field_name=false. Add a pre-pass for Temporal shorthand enum names in history JSON (zig-protobuf returns InvalidEnumTag). Blocked on the map<string,bytes> base64 fix (temporal-sdk-zig-d51.2.6).

title: CI matrix: macOS arm64/x86_64, Linux gnu/musl x86_64/aarch64, Windows x86_64
description: GitHub Actions: build plus unit tests on every platform, and integration tests against a dev server (temporal CLI) on Linux and macOS. Cache cargo target dirs and the zig cache. Also check that the musl static build links.

title: Testing and replay
description: Go testsuite parity on core primitives: dev server and time-skipping test server via core ephemeral servers, a WorkflowEnvironment test harness with activity mocking, an in-process ActivityEnvironment, WorkflowReplayer (JSON/proto histories, from client, batch replay), and determinism-check helpers.

title: Worker: lifecycle, options, tuning, versioning, replayer plumbing
description: temporal.worker.Worker with Go WorkerOptions parity mapped onto TemporalCoreWorkerOptions: registration, poll loops for workflow/activity/nexus, graceful shutdown, tuners/slot suppliers, poller behavior, rate limits, sticky cache, eager activities, worker deployment versioning, task-type toggles, plugins, fatal-error handling, and run-until-interrupt.

title: Activities: execution, heartbeating, cancellation, async completion
description: Run activity tasks from core on the worker's real std.Io (Threaded/Evented): typed dispatch, activity.Context (info, heartbeat, heartbeat details, cancellation, worker-stop signal, client, logger, metrics), async completion, local activities, dynamic activities, struct-method registration.

title: Workflow API surface (Go workflow package parity)
description: User-facing temporal.workflow API on top of the runtime: activities (remote/local), child workflows, timers, signals, queries, updates, external workflow ops, continue-as-new, cancellation, patching/versioning, search attributes/memo, info, side effects, concurrency primitives, dynamic handlers, handler-completion checks, user metadata, priority, workflow versioning behavior.

title: Client: workflow, schedule, deployment, nexus, and service APIs
description: Full Go client.Client parity on top of temporal_core_client_rpc_call: connection options, workflow lifecycle, updates, with-start, history, visibility, async activity completion, standalone activities, standalone nexus operations, schedules, worker deployments and versioning, namespace/operator/cloud access, health check, client interceptors and plugins.

title: Data conversion, payloads, failures, errors
description: Go parity for the converter and temporal packages: DataConverter, PayloadConverters (nil, bytes, protojson, proto, json), PayloadCodec (+zlib), CodecDataConverter, remote codec / codec server HTTP handler, FailureConverter, the error taxonomy, search attributes (typed keys), memo, RawValue, serialization context, external payload storage, and payload limits.
design: JSON via std.json with comptime type info. A type is treated as proto if it has a generated-message marker decl. []const u8 → binary/plain. Optional/null → binary/null. Decoding takes an allocator. EncodedValue/EncodedValues wrappers allow lazy decode (Go converter.EncodedValue parity). Errors: see the root design. Rich failure data travels as temporal.Failure next to narrow Zig error sets.

title: API docs and guides
description: zig autodoc publishing, README, concepts guide (deterministic Io, errors/failures, memory ownership), and migration notes for Go users.

title: Samples mirroring samples-go
description: hello, activity retries, signals/queries/updates, child workflows, saga, cron/schedules, timers, cancellation, local activity, continue-as-new, nexus, mTLS/API key, codec server, replay test, versioning.

title: Zig runner for temporalio/features
description: Implement the features-repo harness for Zig and port the scenarios. This is the objective cross-SDK parity bar.

title: Env config profiles (contrib/envconfig parity)
description: Load TOML/env client profiles through core client_env_config_load, and build ClientOptions from a profile.

title: Context propagators and headers
description: ContextPropagator interface (inject/extract to headers) across client → workflow → activity/child/nexus, Header/WorkflowHeader accessors.

title: Metrics: core exporters, MetricsHandler interface, SDK and workflow metrics
description: Expose core Prometheus/OTLP exporters via runtime options, a temporal.metrics.Handler (counter/gauge/timer with tags) backed by the core meter or custom callbacks, and replay-aware workflow metrics.

title: Worker and client plugins
description: Plugin interface for configuring clients and workers (Go temporal.NewSimplePlugin, worker/client plugin hooks) and reporting plugin info to core.

title: Poller behavior: simple maximum and autoscaling
description: Go NewPollerBehaviorSimpleMaximum/Autoscaling for workflow/activity/nexus pollers, plus the nonsticky-to-sticky ratio.

title: Tuners: fixed, resource-based, composite, custom slot suppliers
description: Go NewFixedSizeTuner, NewResourceBasedTuner, NewCompositeTuner, slot supplier options, ResourceController options, and custom SlotSupplier interface through the bridge.

title: User metadata, current details, priority, versioning intent
description: SetCurrentDetails/GetCurrentDetails, static summary/details on commands, Priority (priority key, fairness key/weight), and WithWorkflowVersioningIntent.

title: SideEffect / MutableSideEffect parity
description: SideEffect implemented as a local activity (core has no generic marker command). Investigate MutableSideEffect: implement if feasible via LA plus patch, otherwise mark as a documented gap. Include DeterministicKeys/sorted-iteration helpers for Zig hash maps.

title: Built-in queries: __stack_trace, __enhanced_stack_trace, __temporal_workflow_metadata
description: Record fiber suspension sites (name plus source location via @src at SDK call sites, or a best-effort return address) for stack trace queries. Workflow metadata reports registered handler definitions and current details.

title: Client outbound interceptor chain
description: ClientInterceptor/ClientOutboundInterceptor parity for every client op, with header propagation.

title: Worker deployment and versioning management APIs
description: WorkerDeploymentClient (List, GetHandle, Delete) and handle ops (Describe, SetCurrentVersion, SetRampingVersion, SetManagerIdentity, DescribeVersion, DeleteVersion, UpdateVersionMetadata). Also legacy DeploymentClient, the build-ID compatibility/versioning rules APIs, DescribeTaskQueue(+Enhanced), and GetWorkerTaskReachability.

title: NamespaceClient and raw service access
description: NamespaceClient (Register/Describe/Update), plus raw WorkflowService/OperatorService (and CloudService) typed stubs exposed to users, like Go client.WorkflowService(). CheckHealth.

title: Standalone activities: ExecuteActivity/GetActivityHandle/List/Count from the client
description: Go's newer client-side activity execution, which runs activities without a workflow. Handle: result, describe, cancel, terminate.

title: Serialization context for converters/codecs
description: Pass a workflow/activity/nexus serialization context (namespace, workflow id, activity type, ...) to context-aware converters and codecs (Go WithDataConverterSerializationContext parity).

title: Custom slot supplier callbacks (reserve/try_reserve/mark_used/release/available)
description: Bridge for user-defined slot suppliers, including async reserve completion via temporal_core_complete_async_reserve / cancel_reserve.

title: Metric meter, attributes, metrics, and custom-meter callbacks
description: Wrap temporal_core_metric_* for SDK-emitted metrics, and the custom meter callback vtable so users can plug a Zig MetricsHandler into core's metrics.

title: Publish prebuilt core static libs per target for Rust-free consumers
description: Release workflow that builds and uploads the c-bridge .a/.lib per tier-1 target and is referenced as a lazy dependency in build.zig.zon (hash-pinned), so `zig fetch` users don't need cargo.

title: Docs, samples, features-harness parity verification, release
description: API docs (zig autodoc), guides, samples mirroring temporalio/samples-go, a Zig runner for temporalio/features as the objective parity bar, a Go-parity checklist, versioning/release process, and package distribution with prebuilt core libs.

title: Observability and extensibility: logging, metrics, tracing, interceptors, plugins
description: Logger interface (std.log bridge, replay-aware), core log forwarding, metrics (core Prometheus/OTLP exporters, custom MetricsHandler via custom meter callbacks, replay-aware workflow metrics), the full interceptor chain (client, workflow inbound/outbound, activity inbound/outbound, nexus), context propagators/headers, a tracing interceptor + OpenTelemetry contrib, and plugins (client/worker SimplePlugin).

title: Nexus: handlers, workflow caller, client operations
description: Go temporalnexus/nexus-rpc parity: service/operation definitions, sync and workflow-run operation handlers, operation tokens and links, the nexus task poll/complete loop, cancellation, workflow-side NexusClient (ScheduleNexusOperation), and client-side standalone nexus operations.

title: Versioning, release, and distribution
description: SemVer policy, changelog, tagging, a build.zig.zon package with prebuilt core libs, and support policy for Zig and core versions.

title: Sessions (Go CreateSession/CompleteSession/RecreateSession/GetSessionInfo)
description: Implement Go's session feature on top of activities and host-specific task queues, with EnableSessionWorker and MaxConcurrentSessionExecutionSize options.

title: contrib/workflowstreams port
description: Durable pub/sub log inside a workflow (signals publish, updates long-poll, query offset), wire-compatible with the Go contrib.

title: Tracing interceptor and OpenTelemetry contrib
description: A generic tracing interceptor (Go interceptor.NewTracingInterceptor parity) plus contrib/opentelemetry span export (OTLP), depending on Zig OTel availability.

title: Sticky cache controls
description: SetStickyWorkflowCacheSize / PurgeStickyWorkflowCache analogs and max_cached_workflows.

title: Workflow-scoped LocalVar (Go NewLocalVar)
description: Workflow-run-scoped typed values for interceptors and libraries, rejected from side-effect/validator contexts.

title: Client-side standalone Nexus operations
description: Go NewNexusClient / GetNexusOperationHandle / ListNexusOperations / CountNexusOperations parity.

title: RawValue and transfer types
description: Pass-through payload values (Go converter.RawValue) and transfer-type converter parity.

title: External payload storage drivers and payload size limits
description: Go converter extstore + PayloadLimits parity: storage-reference payloads, a driver interface, upload/download through the core storage_drivers option where core handles it, preserve-storage-refs decode mode, and warn/error limits (disable_payload_error_limit).

title: Remote codec client and codec-server HTTP handler
description: Go NewRemotePayloadCodec/NewRemoteDataConverter and NewPayloadCodecHTTPHandler parity, so the Temporal UI/CLI can decode payloads through a Zig codec server built on std.http.

title: Advanced and contrib features
description: Go-specific and contrib parity: sessions, workflowstreams, envconfig contrib API, external storage drivers (S3/GCS), lambda/cloudrun workers, sysinfo, workflowcheck-like static determinism lint, and event groups (blocked on core support).

title: Static determinism check (workflowcheck analog)
description: A build-time check that flags non-deterministic calls (std.time, std.crypto.random, direct file/net) reachable from workflow functions, possibly via a comptime/ZIR-based or source-scan tool.

title: Event Groups (Go experimental)
description: Blocked until core exposes an event-group marker command. Track upstream and implement once available.

title: Serverless worker helpers (AWS Lambda, Cloud Run)
description: Go contrib aws/lambdaworker and gcp/cloudrun parity.

title: External storage drivers: S3 and GCS
description: Go contrib aws/s3driver and gcp/gcsdriver parity, using core's aws-s3driver crate where possible.
